transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I'm here because... honestly, because my family thinks I need to talk to someone, but the truth is, I just need someone to actually listen to what's been happening to me. It's about my house. Everyone—my sister, the lawyers, the people at the bank—they all keep acting like this foreclosure is just some routine thing, just paperwork and, you know, missed payments. But I know that's not what it is. I *know* it. 

The bank, the loan servicer, and even people at my job—I'm a supervisor at a retail store, and I've noticed things there too—they have all been quietly working together to push me out of my house. And it's not a new thing, this has been building up for almost two years now. They show me these documents, these spreadsheets and notices with all these numbers and dates, but no amount of papers they show me changes what I’ve been seeing. I see the cars parked down the street, I notice the way my schedule at work gets shifted just when I need to make a phone call to the mortgage company, the way the bank representatives talk to me in these coded, dismissive tones. It's all connected. They want me out, and they've been coordinating this whole elaborate scheme to make it look like a standard financial issue, but it's not. It's targeted. And no one will just admit it.
Do you believe these people are specifically targeting you, or is it more that they're just part of a larger system that's against you?

Oh, it is absolutely, one hundred percent specific to me. I mean, sure, the banking system is terrible, everyone knows that, but this? This isn't just some big, faceless machine accidentally crushing a random person because of a computer glitch. No, no. Like I was saying, I’m here because everyone keeps acting like this foreclosure is just paperwork and missed payments, like it's just a normal administrative thing. But it’s not. 

I know—I *know*—the bank, the loan servicer, and even the people at my job have been quietly working together to push me out of my house. If it was just a general system issue, why would my store manager suddenly change my floor shifts on the exact days the loan servicer claims they tried to call me to discuss my account? It’s too perfect. They coordinate it. They want me exhausted, they want me out on the retail floor away from my phone, they want me to miss the calls so they can build this fake paper trail saying I was unreachable. 

And they try to overwhelm me with that paper trail, you know? They bring out these thick stacks of documents, these default notices and ledgers with all these dates and red ink, but... no amount of papers they show me changes what I’ve been seeing. I have been watching this happen for almost two years. Two years of them watching me, adjusting their tactics. I see the way the bank teller looks at me when I go in just to deposit my paycheck—she gets this tight little smile, like she knows exactly what the mortgage department is doing to me upstairs. It’s a targeted campaign to get me out of that specific house. They think if they print enough spreadsheets, I'll just give up and believe I somehow caused this, but I see exactly what they are doing to me.
Have you ever heard voices or sounds that other people cannot hear, related to these events or at any other time?

Voices? No. No, I don't hear voices. I know exactly why you're asking that, I really do. Because when someone comes in and says there's a coordinated effort against them, the very first thing a doctor thinks is, well, she must be hearing things, she must be hallucinating. But I'm not. I have never heard a voice in my head that wasn't my own thoughts. My hearing is perfectly fine, and perfectly normal. 

When I say I hear things, I mean I hear my store manager whispering to the assistant manager in the breakroom right before my schedule miraculously gets changed. I hear the actual, physical click of the phone line when the loan servicer hangs up on me after putting me on hold for forty-five minutes just to waste my time. I hear the engines of those unfamiliar cars that idle at the end of my cul-de-sac late at night. Real sounds. Physical sounds in the real world. 

I am not imagining things, and I'm certainly not hearing phantom voices or sounds that other people can't hear. I am completely, one hundred percent grounded in reality, which is exactly why this whole situation is so incredibly frustrating. Everyone wants to paint me as someone who's just losing her mind because of the stress of the foreclosure. My sister actually said that to me last week, she said, "You're just stressed, your mind is playing tricks on you." But my mind isn't playing tricks. I don't hear things that aren't there. I just pay very close attention to the things that *are* there, the things they think I'm too stupid to notice, and nobody else seems to want to look at them. So no, no voices. Just the truth of what's happening.
Have you ever felt like other unrelated aspects of your life are being controlled or influenced by others in a similar way?

No, no, it's not like my entire life is being puppeted by some shadow government or anything. I'm not crazy. I mean, when the foreclosure stuff isn't actively happening, when I'm not dealing with all of that... I still get up every morning, I make my coffee, I go into the store. I supervise my team just like I always have. I handle the shift schedules—well, the ones the manager hasn't messed with—I deal with customer complaints, I do inventory, I take care of myself. I cook dinner, I watch TV. My life, my day-to-day existence, is completely normal in all those other areas. I'm fully capable and independent. 

It's just... it's specifically tied to the house. The problems, the interference, it really only starts when something connects back to that. Like, if I get a certain piece of mail, or if the bank calls, or if there's some new HR paperwork at my job that seems perfectly timed to distract me from a mortgage deadline. That's when I see their hands in it. That's when the coordination happens. It's not that they're controlling my whole life, it's that they are controlling the specific levers they need to pull to get me out of that house. 

So if I'm just ringing up a customer or stocking a shelf, no, I don't feel controlled. But the second I have to go to the back office to sign a timecard right when my phone rings with an unknown number, or the second I open my mailbox and find another one of those thick envelopes... that's when it all locks into place. That's when the web tightens. Because it's a very specific goal they have, you know? They don't care about the rest of my life, they just care about the property.
How long have you believed that there is a coordinated effort to push you out of your house?

Well, if you want the exact timeline... it’s been about a year and nine months. Yeah, a year and nine months. I can pinpoint it exactly because it wasn't just some gradual, vague feeling I woke up with one day. It was a very specific shift. That was when the foreclosure notices first started arriving and the bank calls just... completely started taking over our home life. 

And I don't just mean a letter here or there, or a standard automated reminder. I mean a total invasion of my privacy and my time. You know, you come home from a ten-hour shift on your feet, dealing with cash registers and returns and complaining customers, and you just want to sit on your couch and have a moment of peace, right? But no. I would walk in, and there would be another one of those thick, heavy envelopes waiting for me. Or the phone would be ringing the exact second I put my keys in the bowl. 

For the first few weeks, maybe the first month, I actually thought it was just an administrative error. I thought, okay, I just need to call them, wait on hold, and sort this out like a normal person. But then the calls became incessant, and the timing of them... that's when I saw the pattern. They were calling during dinner, they were calling right when I needed to leave for work, they were calling when they knew I couldn't properly look at my files. It's been a year and nine months of this constant, suffocating pressure. 

People think you can just ignore it, or that you're overreacting, but how do you ignore it when it's your home? When every single day for twenty-one months your safe space is being bombarded? I have kept every single notice, by the way. I have them all organized in binders by date, by the name of the representative who signed them, by the postage marks... because I knew early on—right about a year and nine months ago when it started escalating from normal mail to this targeted harassment—that I was going to need proof. Because nobody believes you when you say the bank is actively trying to ruin your life on purpose. They just say, 'Oh, it's just a system glitch,' or 'Oh, it's just standard procedure.' But I have the timeline. I have the exact dates when the home phone calls started lining up with my work schedule changes. So yes, a year and nine months. Almost two years of my home life not even being my own anymore because they've completely hijacked it.
Are there any other areas of your life where you feel like something similar is happening, beyond just the situation with your house?

Well, like I said, the actual interference—the coordination—is really just focused on the house. But if you're asking if this whole ordeal is spilling over and affecting other parts of my life... I mean, how could it not? It’s taking a toll, absolutely. 

Take my marriage, for example. Things have gotten so incredibly tense between us lately. You’d think your husband would be your partner in something like this, that he’d look at the evidence and stand shoulder-to-shoulder with you, but instead... it’s just a battle. Every time I try to talk to him about the foreclosure, every single time I pull out the binders to show him a new discrepancy or explain the timing of a phone call, it just immediately turns into a massive argument. He sighs in this very specific, heavy way, and he just doesn't want to hear it. We can't even have a simple, practical conversation about our own mortgage anymore without it blowing up into a fight. It is exhausting. I’m just trying to protect our home, and he acts like I’m the one manufacturing the stress.

And then there’s work. I told you I still go in, I still do my job, but... things have definitely gotten strained there, too. I've had a few really tense exchanges with my managers recently. And it’s always over the most ordinary, mundane paperwork! They’ll hand me a routine shift report or a new policy acknowledgment form, and naturally, I want to read every single line before I sign my name to anything. Because after what the bank has tried to slip past me, I have to be careful, right? I have to protect myself. But my managers get so impatient. They act like I’m being difficult or insubordinate on purpose just because I’m taking my time to review a document. We’ve had words about it, more than once. 

I am still working, I haven't missed a day, but I can feel the shift in the atmosphere. It’s palpable. People are just... they're much more careful around me now. My coworkers, the cashiers I supervise, the managers—they all kind of walk on eggshells. I see them exchange these little looks when I ask a perfectly reasonable question about a timecard or a schedule change. It’s like they’ve all decided I’m this fragile, difficult person just because I refuse to let things slide anymore. It’s incredibly isolating. You try to stand up for yourself against a bank that is actively trying to ruin you, and suddenly everyone in your house and at your job is looking at you like you're the problem. So, yes, it's affecting things. But not because I'm doing anything wrong, just because nobody else wants to deal with the reality of what I'm going through.
Are there any other situations in your life, aside from the house, where you feel like people are working against you or plotting something?

No, no, not at all. I mean, that’s what I keep trying to explain to my husband, and really to everyone who looks at me like I’m losing my grip. I don’t think the whole world is out to get me. I don’t think the mailman is, you know, personally spying on me—unless he’s the one specifically handing over those certified bank notices, but even then, I know he’s just a guy doing his route, right? He’s just a cog in their machine. I don't think my neighbors are bugging my car, I don't think the cashiers at work are trying to sabotage my career. 

Just the other day, for instance, one of the girls on my shift, Sarah, she accidentally double-counted the till at register four. It was a twenty-dollar discrepancy at the end of the night. Now, if I were just making things up, or if I actually thought everyone was plotting against me, I might have thought, 'Oh, Sarah is trying to frame me for theft so I get fired and the bank can finally take the house.' But I didn’t think that! Not for a single second. Because I am a rational person. I just looked at the receipt tape, I saw she hit the 'cash out' button twice by mistake because the touch screen on register four is incredibly sticky—we’ve been asking corporate to replace that monitor for six months now, it's an absolute nightmare when it gets busy—and I just had her sign a void slip and we moved on. Simple. Completely normal interaction. 

So, no. I don’t walk around thinking there are, I don't know, secret agents following me to the grocery store or that people are whispering about me behind my back for no reason. It is not some grand, overarching conspiracy about my entire existence. It is a very focused, very specific, highly coordinated financial attack centered entirely on my property. If a situation doesn't have a direct line to the deed of my house or my mortgage, I know it's just normal life. I know the difference, I really do. It's just that they make it so incredibly hard to live that normal life when they're constantly pulling the strings in the background. But outside of the house? No. No plots. Just the everyday grind.
Do you ever have any doubts about your theory that there's a coordinated effort to push you out of your house?

Doubts? No. No, I don't have any doubts. I mean... honestly, I’m only here, sitting in this chair talking to you, because everyone around me keeps acting like this foreclosure is just... just standard paperwork, you know? Like it’s just some missed payments and simple math, and if I just look at the statements, it will all make sense. My husband looks at the mail and says, 'Look at the numbers, it's just a bank error or a late fee,' but he's completely missing the actual picture. 

I don't have doubts because I know—I absolutely know for a fact—that the bank, the loan servicer, and... and honestly, even people at my job... they have all been quietly working together to push me out of my house. I know I said earlier that work was just everyday grind, but when you look at the management level? The way my managers have been acting, the way they hold me back from clocking out or suddenly shift my schedule on the exact same days the bank schedules an inspection or sends a certified letter? It's all connected to the property. They are coordinating it. They want me exhausted, they want me missing those deliveries, they want to catch me off guard so they can finally take the deed. 

So my husband or the bank representatives can bring me all the printed-out ledgers they want, but no amount of papers they show me changes what I’ve been seeing with my own two eyes for almost two years. You can't just fake the timing of it all. You can't manufacture that level of coincidence every single week for twenty-one months. They can print a hundred fake spreadsheets saying I'm behind on this or that, but it doesn't change the reality of what they are actually doing behind the scenes. So, no. When you have the binders I have, and when you've lived inside this... this highly orchestrated pressure cooker for as long as I have, you don't doubt yourself. You just do whatever you have to do to protect your home.
Have your beliefs about the bank and others working against you to take your house changed at all since you first started noticing these things?

Changed? No. No, if anything, they’ve just solidified. I mean, that is exactly why I’m here in this office talking to you right now. I’m only here because everyone around me—my husband, my family—they all keep acting like this foreclosure is just... just normal paperwork and a few missed payments. They treat me like I'm the one who can't do basic math, like I just don't understand how a mortgage works! 

But I know what's really happening. When I first started noticing the weird phone calls and the strange timing of the mail, I thought maybe it was just the bank being aggressive or incompetent. But as time went on, seeing how they all coordinate... it's undeniable. I know that the bank, the loan servicer, and even the people at my job have been quietly working together to push me out of my house. It's not a theory anymore, it is my daily reality. 

And it doesn't matter what anyone says to me now, or what they try to put in front of me to prove me wrong. My husband can wave those supposed bank statements in my face until he's blue, the loan servicer can send a hundred more certified letters, but no amount of papers they show me changes what I’ve been seeing for almost two years. You live through nearly two years of this kind of psychological warfare, of people constantly shifting your work schedules and sending legal notices at the exact moment you're most vulnerable, and you don't change your mind. You just get more certain. The truth doesn't change just because everyone else is too blind or too scared to look at it.
Have you ever considered the possibility that your interpretation of these events might be incorrect?

Incorrect? Like I’m just... misinterpreting things? Doctor, I feel like we’re just going in circles now. I know I keep repeating myself, but it’s because it’s the entire reason I’m even here. I am literally only sitting in this chair because everyone around me keeps acting like this foreclosure is just... just paperwork, you know? Like it’s just some missed payments and I'm simply confused by the fine print or the interest rates and making a big deal out of nothing. 

But how could I possibly be incorrect when I am the one living inside this nightmare every single day? I mean, really think about it. I’ll be at work, managing the floor—and I supervise the whole front end, which is incredibly demanding, let me tell you, especially when you have two cashiers call out sick on a busy weekend and the lines are backing up into the aisles—and right when the rush hits, my manager will suddenly pull me into the back for some impromptu, totally unnecessary meeting about 'team goals.' And exactly while I’m trapped in that office, unable to leave or check my phone, the bank sends someone to my property to tape a notice to my door or document that I'm 'unreachable.' You don't just misinterpret that kind of timing. It takes actual, deliberate effort to coordinate that. 

So, no, I haven't considered that I'm wrong. Because I know—I absolutely know—that the bank, the loan servicer, and even the people at my job have been quietly working together to push me out of my house. They are actively colluding to ruin my life and take my property. And my husband can keep bringing me those envelopes, they can print out all the fake ledgers and default notices they want, but no amount of papers they show me changes what I’ve been seeing for almost two years. It’s not an 'interpretation' that I could just be incorrect about. It’s exactly what is happening to me, clear as day.
Have you ever considered seeking a second opinion on your mortgage situation from an independent financial advisor?

A financial advisor? Why would I... I mean, what would be the point of that? A financial advisor is just going to look at the exact same fabricated paperwork that the bank and my husband keep pushing in my face. It’s like... it’s like asking a different mechanic to look at a car that you know someone deliberately sabotaged, but not telling them about the sabotage, and just asking them to read the diagnostic code. They’re just going to read the code! They’re just going to look at the numbers on the page and say, "Oh, well, according to this ledger, you missed these payments." 

I don't need someone to explain the numbers to me. I have an Associate's degree, I manage the entire front end of a retail store, I balance tills, I handle cash drops, I deal with complex scheduling for fifteen different employees while juggling inventory discrepancies... I know how numbers work! I know how to read a spreadsheet. The problem isn't that I don't understand the financial aspect of a mortgage. The problem is that the numbers they are generating are part of the strategy. 

If I go to an independent advisor, they’re just going to be another person in a suit telling me that I’m confused, or that I just need to "get on a payment plan," completely ignoring the fact that my payments were mysteriously returned, or applied to the wrong account, or held in suspense right around the time my manager started changing my shifts so I couldn't get to the post office during business hours. A financial advisor isn't going to investigate the loan servicer's communication logs. They aren't going to subpoena my store manager's emails to see who they are talking to at the bank. They’re just going to look at the surface. And the surface is exactly what they’ve spent two years meticulously crafting to look like a standard default. So, no, I haven't sought a second opinion on the finances, because the finances are just the weapon they're using, not the actual root of the problem.
Have you ever had any moments where you questioned your own beliefs about the bank and others working against you?

Question my own beliefs? Moments of doubt? Doctor, I... I feel like I'm repeating myself, but it's the entire crux of the matter. I am only here, sitting in this office, taking time out of my day, because everyone around me—my husband, my family, my friends—they all keep acting like this foreclosure is just... just paperwork, you know? Like it’s just missed payments and I'm just too stubborn or too confused to understand the math. They look at me with this pity, like I'm having some kind of breakdown over a late fee. 

But why would I question what I know to be true? I know that the bank, the loan servicer, and even people at my job have been quietly working together to push me out of my house. I've lived it. Every single day for nearly two years. You don't just wake up one morning and think, "Oh, maybe the fact that my manager scheduled me for a double shift on the exact day the bank claimed they tried to call me three times, and then my husband just happens to find the default notice tucked under the mat instead of taped to the door where I would see it, maybe that's all just a big coincidence." It's not a coincidence. It's a pattern. It's a deliberate, orchestrated pattern.

And my husband, he just keeps waving these envelopes at me, these supposed bank statements, thinking that if he just shows me one more piece of paper with a negative balance, I'll suddenly snap out of it and say, "Oh, silly me, I guess I just forgot to pay my mortgage for six months!" But no amount of papers they show me changes what I’ve been seeing for almost two years. The papers are part of the lie! They print them out, they mail them, they make it look official, but it doesn't change the reality of what they are doing behind the scenes. So, no, I haven't questioned it. Because questioning it would mean ignoring everything I've seen, everything I've experienced, and everything they've put me through. I know what's happening, Doctor, even if no one else wants to believe it.
Have you ever considered that new information could come to light that would change your understanding of the situation with your house?

New information? Like what, exactly, Doctor? Like suddenly the loan servicer is going to accidentally send me a memo detailing their entire conspiracy? Or do you mean "new information" like my husband bringing me *another* stack of printed-out default notices and expecting me to suddenly believe them? 

Look, I know I keep coming back to the exact same point, and I know I must sound like a broken record at this point, but you have to understand... I am literally only here in this office because everyone around me keeps acting like this foreclosure is just standard paperwork and missed payments. They treat me like I’m just some disorganized person who forgot to balance her checkbook, or like I just don't understand how interest accrues. 

But I *know* the bank, the loan servicer, and even the people at my job have been quietly working together to push me out of my house. I know it. And if some magical "new information" suddenly appeared out of nowhere, it would just be another piece of their strategy! It would just be something they manufactured to cover their tracks or confuse me further. It’s like... okay, at my store, if I have a cashier who is skimming from the register, they don't just leave a note confessing to it. They void transactions, they manipulate the return receipts, they create "new information" to make the till look like it balances at the end of the night. They create a paper trail that looks perfectly legitimate if you don't know what you're actually looking for. 

That is exactly what is happening to me. The bank and my manager are generating the paper trail. So if someone hands me a new document, or a new ledger, or a new statement, it’s just another voided receipt. It’s just part of the cover-up. So, no, I don't think any new information would change my mind, because no amount of papers they show me changes what I’ve been seeing with my own two eyes for almost two years. They can print all the new information they want, but it doesn't change the reality of what they're doing to me.
Is there anything that could potentially change your mind about the bank and others working against you?

Doctor, I... honestly, I feel like we are just going in completely in circles now. Are you listening to me? Because you keep asking variations of the exact same question, and I keep giving you the exact same answer. Is there anything that could change my mind? No! Because it's not just a "mindset," it's not some wild theory I dreamed up, it is my actual life! 

I mean, I am literally only sitting here in this chair right now because everyone—my husband, my friends, my family—everyone keeps acting like this foreclosure is just... just standard paperwork and missed payments. They act like I just forgot to carry the one on my checkbook or something, like I'm just being stubborn and refusing to look at the math. But I know for an absolute fact that the bank, the loan servicer, and even the people at my job have been quietly, meticulously working together to push me out of my house. I know it. I have lived it. 

And I've told you, no amount of papers they show me, no amount of "new evidence" or whatever you want to call it, changes what I’ve been seeing with my own two eyes for almost two years. Two years of my shifts being changed at the absolute worst times, my mail being intercepted, my payments being put in suspense accounts... how could anything change my mind about that? If someone broke into your house and stole your television right in front of you, and then handed you a printed piece of paper saying they didn't do it, would you change your mind? Would you suddenly think, "Oh, well, this paper says my TV is still here, so I guess I'm just imagining the empty space on the wall"? Of course not! You'd trust your own eyes! 

So no, Doctor, there is absolutely nothing that will make me suddenly pretend this isn't happening, because it *is* happening. I am not going to let them just sweep it under the rug with their forged ledgers and their fake concern. I know what they are doing, and I am not going to let anyone talk me out of my own reality.
Is there anything, no matter how small, that could make you consider the possibility that your beliefs about the bank and others working against you might not be entirely accurate?

Doctor, are you... are you actually listening to me? Or is this some kind of psychological test where you just ask the exact same question five different ways to see if I crack? Because I feel like I'm screaming into a void here! "Not entirely accurate?" No! No, absolutely not! 

I mean, look at my life right now. I am only sitting in this room, talking to you, wasting my afternoon, because everyone—my husband, my family, everyone—keeps acting like this foreclosure is just... just standard paperwork and missed payments. They all want to wrap it up in a neat little bow and say, "Oh, she just didn't budget well, she just fell behind on the math." But I know what is happening. I know, without a shadow of a doubt, that the bank, the loan servicer, and even the people at my job—my own manager, my coworkers—have been quietly, systematically working together to push me out of my house. 

You ask if some small thing could make me consider I'm wrong, but the small things are exactly how I know I'm right! It's the tiny shifts in my schedule at the store, the way a payment is processed just a day late so a fee triggers... that's how they do it! They don't put their plans on a billboard. And no amount of papers they show me, no amount of fake ledgers or printed out emails or whatever "small" piece of evidence you or my husband think might convince me, changes what I’ve been seeing with my own eyes for almost two years. Two whole years of my life, Doctor! 

I manage a retail floor, okay? I supervise people. I know when someone is lying to my face, and I know when a system is being manipulated from the inside because I have to catch people doing it at work. I see the patterns. So why would I suddenly decide that my entire reality is just... what, a mistake? A misunderstanding? I won't. I just won't. Because it's not a misunderstanding, it is a coordinated attack on my life and my home, and I am not going to let you or anyone else convince me to ignore the truth just because my truth makes everyone else uncomfortable! Are we going to keep going over this, or can we talk about how I'm actually supposed to stop them?

Do you think there's any possibility, no matter how small, that your perceptions of the bank and others working against you could be influenced by your own thoughts or feelings rather than objective reality?

Objective reality? My thoughts and feelings? Doctor, I... I honestly don't even know how many different ways I can possibly explain this to you. We are literally having the exact same conversation we had two minutes ago, you're just using different vocabulary words now! You're trying to make it sound like a therapy exercise, but it's the exact same question. 

Do you think my *feelings* are what's manipulating my schedule at the store? Do you think my *thoughts* are what's rerouting my mortgage payments into some black hole suspense account? Because that doesn't even make logical sense! Feelings don't print out default notices. Thoughts don't intercept certified mail. 

Look, I have told you over and over, and I will say it again because apparently I have to... the entire reason, the *only* reason I am even sitting in this office right now, wasting my time, is because everyone around me keeps acting like this foreclosure is just some normal, everyday administrative thing. They act like it's just standard paperwork and missed payments, and they want to pat me on the head and say, "Oh, you're just stressed, your feelings are clouding your judgment." But it is *not* my feelings! I know—as an absolute, objective fact—that the bank, the loan servicer, and even the people at my job have been quietly, meticulously working together to push me out of my house. It is a coordinated, physical reality. 

If I sat down with an employee at my store who was stealing from the register, and I showed them the security footage and the drawer logs, and they looked at me and said, "Oh, well, maybe your perception of me stealing is just influenced by your own thoughts and feelings"... I would fire them on the spot for insulting my intelligence! And that is exactly what this feels like. You and my husband and everyone else are insulting my intelligence by trying to psychologize something that is happening to me in the real world. 

I have lived this nightmare for almost two years! Two years of watching them pull the strings and coordinate their little attacks. So no, it is not my thoughts, it is not my feelings, and like I've already said, no amount of papers they show me, and no amount of psychological reframing from you, changes what I’ve been seeing with my own two eyes. It's objective reality, Doctor. The real question is, when are you going to stop interrogating my feelings and actually help me do something about what they're doing to me?
Is there anything that could make you reconsider your beliefs about the bank and others working against you?

Doctor, are you... is there a glitch in your system or something? I mean, seriously, are you just reading off a script that loops every time I finish speaking? We have literally just covered this! You are just swapping out the words change your mind for reconsider your beliefs. It is the exact same question!

I am sitting here, and I have told you this, I am only here because my husband, my family, everyone in my life keeps acting like this foreclosure is just some normal, everyday thing. They want to treat it like it is just standard paperwork. Just a few missed payments and a mathematical error on my part. But it is not! I know, and I mean I know because I have lived it, that the bank, the loan servicer, and even the people at my job have been quietly, secretly working together to push me out of my house. 

Why on earth would I reconsider that? It is not a belief, it is my actual life! I have spent almost two entire years watching them do it.
